newsitem.title: USA: US Senate rejects cut in MAP funding in FY98.
newsitem.headline: US Senate rejects cut in MAP funding in FY98.

text.p: The U.S. Senate rejected a proposal on Wednesday to reduce funding for the Market Access Program to $70 million in fiscal 1998.
Senator Richard Bryan, Nevada Democrat, proposed a $20 million cut in funding for MAP, arguing the cost-sharing program was a waste of tax dollars.
The program awards grants to commodity groups, co-ops and small businesses to aid in developing markets for U.S. ag exports.
Mississippi Republican Thad Cochran said the program was unfairly criticized and had a solid record of boosting exports.
"The program is working," Lott said. "It's not being abused anymore -- if it ever was."
In addition to the cut in funds, Bryan wanted to alter the program to make sure that foreign firms would have no contact with funds, even indirectly through subsidiaries.
